precepts.text: Israel falls by the edge of Rome's sword, is led captive into all nations, and Jerusalem is trodden down of the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled: the strange slips.
precepts.point: Thou shalt plant pleasant plants and set it with strange slips: a slip is a cutting from a plant, so strange branches, Esau, not the people of the covenant, set in the land.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
“In that day shall his strong cities be as a forsaken bough, and an uppermost branch, which they left because of the children of Israel: and there shall be desolation.” We were moved out of the land. Why? “Because thou hast forgotten the God of thy salvation, and hast not been mindful of the rock of thy strength.” We have not been mindful of him. “Therefore shalt thou plant pleasant plants, and shalt set it with strange slips.”

What is a slip? A cutting from a plant, a branch or twig. Strange slips are strange branches: Esau. They are strange, not the people of the book, not the people of the covenant, set into the land. Christ said the same thing about strange slips coming into the land.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the real Israelites fell by the edge of Rome's sword. “And shall be led away captive into all nations”: captive means slaves, carried into all nations.

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” Christ is telling you the Gentiles are going to take over the land. That is what Isaiah said about the strange slips, the strange people who would take the land while the real children of Israel were scattered. And these leaders who bring out that they are not the real Jews disappear and die; we are the last ones standing.

precepts.text: I will bring the worst of the heathen and they shall possess their houses; mischief upon mischief and rumour upon rumour.
precepts.point: Thou shalt plant pleasant plants and set it with strange slips: a slip is a cutting from a plant, so strange branches, Esau, not the people of the covenant, set in the land.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the land would be set “with strange slips”, and Christ says Jerusalem would be “trodden down of the Gentiles.” Ezekiel gives another precept on who those strangers are.

“Wherefore I will bring the worst of the heathen, and they shall possess their houses.” God calls them the worst of the heathen, and they will possess our houses. Those are the Gentiles Christ was speaking about in Luke 21:24, the strange slips planted in our land.

“I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease; and their holy places shall be defiled. Destruction cometh; and they shall seek peace, and there shall be none. Mischief shall come upon mischief, and rumour shall be upon rumour.”

That is what we see now. America and Israel fund rebel forces and put a former al-Qaeda commander, Abu Mohammad al-Jolani, once with a ten-million-dollar bounty on his head, in as president of Syria, because Assad said they are not even real Jews and shouldn't be in the land; now Trump shakes his hand in the White House. Israel announces it will occupy southern Lebanon up to the Litani River. Mischief upon mischief and rumour upon rumour: the worst of the heathen possessing the houses of the children of Israel.

precepts.text: Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the seas, and to the rushing of nations like mighty waters; God shall rebuke them and they shall flee like chaff. The waves that roar in Jeremiah 51:55 are the nations within Babylon.
precepts.point: The serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the woman. His mouth is the media, every aspect of it so-called Jewish owned, and the water is lies. The flood is to draw the twelve tribes into Christian and democratic lies.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
Jeremiah 51:55 says “when her waves do roar like great waters, a noise of their voice is uttered”. The waves that roar are the nations, and Isaiah 17 is the precept that proves it.

“Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” The nations are the waters, making a noise like the seas.

“The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters: but God shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thing before the whirlwind.”

So the waters in these prophecies are peoples and nations. The waves roaring within Babylon are the nations inside her, and however they rush, God will rebuke them and chase them like chaff before the wind.

precepts.text: The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters, but God shall rebuke them.
precepts.point: Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers. Our help is in the name of the Lord.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
Psalms 124 goes on: “Then they had swallowed us up quick”, the nations would have swallowed us up, “Then the waters had overwhelmed us, the stream had gone over our soul:” “Then the proud waters had gone over our soul.” The waters are not the water of affliction. Write it down, brothers: the waters in Psalms 124 are the nations.

Isaiah proves it: “Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” Keep reading: “The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters”. He is comparing the nations to waters.

“but God shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thing before the whirlwind.” That is the Lord being on our side: the proud waters, the nations, rush against Israel, and God rebukes them.

precepts.point: The new heaven is the kingdom.
